messages.speaker: Professor Chen
messages.text: Fourth protocol. I want to confirm my theory: the creature does not react to your acts, but to your representations.

messages.speaker: Professor Chen
messages.text: You will only imagine a scene. No bulkhead will move. No technician will be exposed.

choices.label: I imagine a threat behind the glass and prepare to retaliate.
I imagine the sensors and keep the scene abstract.
I imagine a safe exit so it does not feel trapped.

messages.speaker: Professor Chen
messages.text: It reacted as if your scene had just happened. The spectrogram shows a genomic surge, but the room is intact.

messages.speaker: Professor Chen
messages.text: Next dilemma: if it believes fiction, do you have the right to lie to calm it?

choices.label: Yes, if the lie prevents a dangerous mutation.
No. Calming it with falsehood builds it an unstable world.
I test a simple fiction to understand its limits.

messages.speaker: Professor Chen
messages.text: The bioelectric spectrogram analysis is clear: its genome moves during your hypotheses. Sometimes it shows on its body, sometimes it does not.

messages.speaker: Professor Chen
messages.text: It does not understand our notion of imagination. What you imagine, it treats as a reality to survive.

choices.label: Then we ban violent scenarios around it.
We use controlled images to teach it nuance.
We explore this mental language before the outside signal does.
